Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Soderberg Relation: $\frac{\sigma_a}{S_e} + \frac{\sigma_m}{S_y} = \frac{1}{n}$ (Most conservative; guards against yielding)
  • Goodman Relation: $\frac{\sigma_a}{S_e} + \frac{\sigma_m}{S_{ut}} = \frac{1}{n}$ (Standard for ductile materials)
  • Gerber Parabolic Criterion: $\frac{n \sigma_a}{S_e} + \left(\frac{n \sigma_m}{S_{ut}}\right)^2 = 1$
  • Marin Endurance Limit Modifiers: $S_e = k_a k_b k_c k_d k_e S_e'$ (Surface, size, load, temp, reliability factors)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Stress Concentration ($K_t$ vs $K_f$): Fatigue notch factor $K_f = 1 + q(K_t - 1)$, where $q$ is notch sensitivity ($0 \le q \le 1$).
  • Reversed vs Fluctuating Stress: Completely reversed has $\sigma_m = 0$; fluctuating has both non-zero mean and alternating components.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Soderberg line connects $S_e$ on vertical axis to $S_y$ on horizontal axis.
  • Endurance limit of steel is approximately $S_e' \approx 0.5 S_{ut}$ for $S_{ut} \le 1400$ MPa.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • High-Cycle Fatigue Design Principles

1. Fluctuating Stress Formulations & Failure Hypotheses

Machine elements subjected to cyclic loading fail at stresses far below static yield strength due to microcrack initiation and propagation. Evaluating safe combinations of alternating stress $\sigma_a = (\sigma_{\max} - \sigma_{\min})/2$ and mean stress $\sigma_m = (\sigma_{\max} + \sigma_{\min})/2$ ensures infinite life design.

$$\frac{\sigma_a}{S_e} + \frac{\sigma_m}{S_{ut}} = \frac{1}{n}, \quad S_e = 0.5 S_{ut} \cdot k_{\text{surf}} k_{\text{size}} k_{\text{rel}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Automotive engine connecting rods, railway axle shafts, and wind turbine rotor blades.

Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Primary Direct Shear Load: $F_1 = \frac{P}{n}$ (uniform on each of $n$ bolts in group)
  • Secondary Torsional Shear Load: $F_{2i} = \frac{P \cdot e \cdot r_i}{\sum r_j^2}$ (perpendicular to radius vector $r_i$ from centroid)
  • Resultant Critical Bolt Load: $F_R = \sqrt{F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2 F_1 F_2 \cos\theta}$
  • Bolt Core Diameter Stress: $\sigma = \frac{P_b}{\frac{\pi}{4} d_c^2}$, where $d_c \approx 0.84 d$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Bolt Preload Tightening: Initial tightening tension $F_i \approx 0.75 A_t S_p$ prevents joint separation and improves fatigue resistance.
  • Joint Stiffness Factor ($C$): $C = \frac{k_b}{k_b + k_m}$, Total bolt load $P_b = F_i + C P$.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Critical bolt is the one with maximum resultant vector sum ($F_1 + F_2$), having minimum angle $\theta$ between vectors.
  • Gasketed joints typically require high clamp stiffness to prevent fluid leakage under internal pressure.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Bolted Joint Mechanics & Eccentric Loading

1. In-Plane & Out-of-Plane Eccentric Fastener Design

When external load $P$ acts at eccentric distance $e$ from the centroid of a bolt pattern, it induces direct shear plus twisting moment $M = P \cdot e$. Each bolt experiences primary shear along load line plus secondary shear proportional to radial distance.

$$F_{2} = \frac{P e r}{\sum r_i^2}, \quad F_{\max} = \sqrt{F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2 F_1 F_2 \cos\theta} \le \tau_{\text{allow}} \frac{\pi d_c^2}{4}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Structural crane brackets, column-beam bracket connections, and gearbox flange bolting.

Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Fillet Weld Throat Thickness: $t = h \cdot \cos(45^\circ) = 0.707 h$ (where $h$ is weld leg size)
  • Transverse Fillet Weld Strength: $P = 0.707 h L \sigma_t$ (Transverse weld is ~17% stronger than parallel weld)
  • Parallel Fillet Weld Strength: $P = 2 \times (0.707 h L \tau) = 1.414 h L \tau$ (Double parallel fillet)
  • Riveted Joint Efficiency ($\eta$): $\eta = \frac{\min(P_t, P_s, P_c)}{P_{\text{solid plate}}} = \frac{\min(P_t, P_s, P_c)}{p \cdot t \cdot \sigma_t}$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Weld Failure Plane: Fillet welds are assumed to fail in shear across the minimum throat cross-section inclined at $45^\circ$.
  • Riveted Joint Failure Modes: Tearing of plate between rivets ($P_t = (p-d)t\sigma_t$); Shearing of rivets ($P_s = n \frac{\pi d^2}{4}\tau$); Crushing/bearing of plate ($P_c = n d t \sigma_c$).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • In circular fillet welds under torsion: polar moment of unit weld $J_u = 2\pi r^3$.
  • Welded joints provide 100% joint efficiency, leak tightness, and lighter weight compared to riveted joints.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Welded Connection Sizing & Stress Analysis

1. Fillet Weld Stresses Under Static & Cyclic Loads

Regardless of whether external loading is tension, compression, or shear, fillet welds are evaluated based on shear stress acting across the minimum effective throat section $t = 0.707 h$.

$$\tau = \frac{P}{0.707 h L}, \quad \text{Torsional Weld: } \tau_2 = \frac{T \cdot r}{0.707 h J_u}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Heavy industrial gantry girders, pressure piping header branch welds, and offshore platform jackets.

Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Maximum Shear Stress (Wahl): $\tau_{\max} = K_w \frac{8 F D}{\pi d^3}$ (where $F$ is load, $D$ mean coil diameter, $d$ wire diameter)
  • Spring Index ($C$): $C = D / d$ (Optimum range $C = 6 \text{ to } 9$)
  • Wahl Stress Factor ($K_w$): $K_w = \frac{4C-1}{4C-4} + \frac{0.615}{C}$ (Accounts for direct shear and coil wire curvature)
  • Axial Deflection ($\delta$): $\delta = \frac{8 F D^3 n}{G d^4}$ (where $n$ is active coils, $G$ shear modulus)
  • Spring Stiffness / Rate ($k$): $k = \frac{F}{\delta} = \frac{G d^4}{8 D^3 n}$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Surging in Springs: Resonant standing waves when cyclic loading frequency matches fundamental natural frequency $f_n = \frac{d}{2\pi D^2 n}\sqrt{\frac{G}{2\rho}}$.
  • Springs in Series vs Parallel: Series: $1/k_{eq} = 1/k_1 + 1/k_2$ (deflections add); Parallel: $k_{eq} = k_1 + k_2$ (loads add).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Curvature effect significantly increases shear stress on the INNER fiber of the spring wire.
  • Shot peening introduces beneficial compressive residual surface stresses, increasing fatigue life.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Spring Mechanics & High-Duty Coil Design

1. Curvature & Direct Shear Correction in Helical Springs

Twisting of helical wire produces torsional shear stress $\tau = Tr/J$. Due to coil helix curvature, the path length on the inner fiber is shorter, amplifying stress concentration captured by A.M. Wahl's analytical factor.

$$\tau_{\max} = \left( \frac{4C-1}{4C-4} + \frac{0.615}{C} \right) \frac{8 F D}{\pi d^3}, \quad U = \frac{1}{2} F \delta = \frac{4 F^2 D^3 n}{G d^4}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: IC engine valve springs, railway wagon bogie suspensions, and precision pressure relief valves.

Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Lamé's Equations: Radial stress $\sigma_r = A - \frac{B}{r^2}$; Hoop stress $\sigma_\theta = A + \frac{B}{r^2}$
  • Boundary Conditions: At inner radius $r = r_i$: $\sigma_r = -p_i$; At outer radius $r = r_o$: $\sigma_r = -p_o$
  • Internal Pressure Only ($p_o = 0$): $\sigma_{\theta,\max} = p_i \left(\frac{r_o^2 + r_i^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2}\right)$ at inner bore $r = r_i$
  • Auto-Frettage & Compounding: Shrink-fit of outer jacket over inner cylinder induces beneficial compressive hoop prestress at inner bore.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Thick Cylinder Criterion: Wall thickness $t > d_i / 20$; radial stress is significant and hoop stress is non-uniform.
  • Maximum Shear Stress: $\tau_{\max} = \frac{\sigma_\theta - \sigma_r}{2} = \frac{B}{r^2}$ (Absolute peak at inner surface).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Hoop stress $\sigma_\theta$ is always MAXIMUM at inner radius $r_i$ and MINIMUM at outer radius $r_o$.
  • In compound cylinders, the interface shrinkage pressure prestresses the inner bore into compression.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Thick Shell Mechanics & Autofrettage

1. Lamé Formulation for Axisymmetric Thick Cylinders

Setting up radial equilibrium $\frac{d\sigma_r}{dr} + \frac{\sigma_r - \sigma_\theta}{r} = 0$ and plane strain longitudinal displacement compatibility yields hyperbolic radial and circumferential stress fields.

$$\sigma_\theta(r) = \frac{p_i r_i^2 - p_o r_o^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2} + \frac{r_i^2 r_o^2 (p_i - p_o)}{r^2 (r_o^2 - r_i^2)}, \quad \sigma_r(r) = \frac{p_i r_i^2 - p_o r_o^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2} - \frac{r_i^2 r_o^2 (p_i - p_o)}{r^2 (r_o^2 - r_i^2)}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: High pressure chemical reactor autoclaves, artillery gun barrels, and deep ocean submersible hulls.

1. Lamé Formulation for Axisymmetric Thick Cylinders

Setting up radial equilibrium $\frac{d\sigma_r}{dr} + \frac{\sigma_r - \sigma_\theta}{r} = 0$ and plane strain longitudinal displacement compatibility yields hyperbolic radial and circumferential stress fields.

$$\sigma_\theta(r) = \frac{p_i r_i^2 - p_o r_o^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2} + \frac{r_i^2 r_o^2 (p_i - p_o)}{r^2 (r_o^2 - r_i^2)}, \quad \sigma_r(r) = \frac{p_i r_i^2 - p_o r_o^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2} - \frac{r_i^2 r_o^2 (p_i - p_o)}{r^2 (r_o^2 - r_i^2)}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: High pressure chemical reactor autoclaves, artillery gun barrels, and deep ocean submersible hulls.

Exam Mode Scoring Summary & Key Formulas

⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET501 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Lamé's Equations: Radial stress $\sigma_r = A - \frac{B}{r^2}$; Hoop stress $\sigma_\theta = A + \frac{B}{r^2}$
  • Boundary Conditions: At inner radius $r = r_i$: $\sigma_r = -p_i$; At outer radius $r = r_o$: $\sigma_r = -p_o$
  • Internal Pressure Only ($p_o = 0$): $\sigma_{\theta,\max} = p_i \left(\frac{r_o^2 + r_i^2}{r_o^2 - r_i^2}\right)$ at inner bore $r = r_i$
  • Auto-Frettage & Compounding: Shrink-fit of outer jacket over inner cylinder induces beneficial compressive hoop prestress at inner bore.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Thick Cylinder Criterion: Wall thickness $t > d_i / 20$; radial stress is significant and hoop stress is non-uniform.
  • Maximum Shear Stress: $\tau_{\max} = \frac{\sigma_\theta - \sigma_r}{2} = \frac{B}{r^2}$ (Absolute peak at inner surface).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Hoop stress $\sigma_\theta$ is always MAXIMUM at inner radius $r_i$ and MINIMUM at outer radius $r_o$.
  • In compound cylinders, the interface shrinkage pressure prestresses the inner bore into compression.
